Series::log10¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series::log10() const -> Series
Series& Series::log10_()
Series& Series::log10_() const

What It Does¶

log10() is the base-10 logarithm, applied elementwise: log10(x) is the power to which 10 must be raised to get x.

Base 10 is the readable choice when the answer is an order of magnitude — a decibel level, a pH, the number of digits in an integer, an axis tick on a log-scaled plot.

Anchor values: log10(1) = 0, log10(10) = 1, log10(100) = 2, log10(0.1) = -1.

Domain:

  • x > 0 gives an ordinary result

  • x = 0 gives -inf

  • x < 0 gives NaN

An integer input is promoted to a floating-point result.

Parameters¶

None.

Returns¶

Series or Series& The base-10 logarithm elementwise. log10_() overwrites the current storage.

Gradient¶

log10() is differentiable:

d/dx log10(x) = 1 / (x * ln 10)

That is the natural-log derivative 1/x scaled by 1 / ln 10 (about 0.4343).

In-Place Form¶

log10_() is the in-place sibling of log10(): it computes the same result and writes it back into self directly — mutating it (and any other handle sharing the same storage) instead of allocating a new Series — then returns a reference to self.

Despite being declared const at the call site — a quirk of how this method’s wrapper is generated, not a promise that self is left unchanged — log10_() genuinely mutates the series it’s called on.

auto x = pluss::make_series({1.0, 10.0, 100.0});

auto& ref = x.log10_();
std::cout << "x=" << x << "\n";
std::cout << std::boolalpha << "same object: " << (&ref == &x);

Output¶

x=pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[0, 1, 2]
same object: true

Examples¶

Example 1. Powers of ten map to integers.

pluss::series::print(
    std::cout,
    pluss::make_series({1.0, 10.0, 100.0, 0.1}).log10());

Output¶

Series(shape=[4], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[0.0000, 1.0000, 2.0000, -1.0000]

Example 2. The backward multiplier is 1 / (x * ln 10).

auto x = pluss::make_series({1.0, 10.0, 100.0});
x.tracks_slope_(true);

x.log10().sum().reverse();

std::cout << "dx=" << x.sensitivity();

Output¶

dx=pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[0.43429448, 0.043429448, 0.0043429448]

Each entry is 0.43429448 / x, since 1 / ln 10 = 0.43429448.

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • log10(0) is -inf and log10(x < 0) is NaN; neither throws.

  • The result is floating point even for an integer input.

  • For a natural-log quantity use log(); for base 2 use log2().

Summary¶

log10(x) is the base-10 logarithm:

  • -inf at 0, NaN for negatives

  • promotes integer input to floating point

  • differentiable, backward multiplier 1 / (x * ln 10)

See Also¶

  • Series::log: natural logarithm; base-10 is this scaled by 1 / ln 10.

  • Series::log2: base-2 logarithm.

  • Series::exp: to go the other way, since 10^x = exp(x * ln 10).
